extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and patent practitioners who practice before the USPTO (and those responding to USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline investigations)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, regulatory requirements, and remedial obligations applicable to attorneys practicing before the USPTO, especially rules on handling client funds, timely payment of USPTO fees, supervision, document integrity, and disciplinary procedures and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve identity of client funds and property (37 C.F.R. § 10.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must preserve the identity of client funds and property and not deposit client funds into the firm's operating account such that client funds are indistinguishable from firm funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page examples: Respondent deposited (1) earned fees, (2) unearned fees, and (3) funds his clients gave him to pay USPTO fees into a single firm operating account rather than into one or more separate accounts for each client's funds. The Third Response failed to present documentary evidence showing that Respondent maintained his clients' funds separate from his firm's funds or individual clients' funds separate from one another. Reliance on state ethics opinions does not answer whether conduct violates USPTO regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No commingling of client funds (best practice / regulatory requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Client funds intended for government filing fees or other client-specific purposes must not be commingled with the attorney's business operating funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete anti-pattern: depositing government filing-fee payments into an operating account and later using that account to pay USPTO fees, resulting in dishonored checks. Remedial practice on this page: open/maintain a USPTO Deposit Account and keep minimum balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely payment of USPTO fees; issue fee timing (35 U.S.C. § 151)
rubrics_metrics.description: An issue fee must be paid in all allowed patent applications within three months of a written notice of allowance; if not timely paid the application is regarded as abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issue fee not paid timely, revival is possible only if 'delay in payment is shown to have been unavoidable' via petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.137(a), filed with delayed fee and petition fees. The Final Order recounts a case where filing and payment after deadline but without a petition did not cure abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: File petition to revive for unavoidable delay when fees/filings are late (37 C.F.R. § 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Late payments or filings that caused abandonment may be cured only by filing the delayed fee along with a petition to revive for unavoidable delay and payment of the petition fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: submitting replacement check months after due date without accompanying petition; USPTO may cash the check but absence of petition/foundations means the abandonment remains and the remedy is not properly effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit checks drawn on insufficient funds; consequences under fitness standard (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting checks to the USPTO that are dishonored for insufficient funds or uncollected funds holds constitutes conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice and violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint identifies 23 dishonored checks totaling $7,705.00. When a check is dishonored, the practitioner must pay the fee or fee+processing fee required by USPTO regulation (see 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m)). Repeated or systemic dishonored checks are an aggravating misconduct factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay the $50 processing fee for dishonored checks (37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a check submitted to the USPTO is dishonored, the practitioner must pay the underlying fee plus the processing fee required under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m) (the order records numerous payments of the $50 fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For each dishonored check the Respondent later paid the underlying fee and the $50 processing fee. Best practice: ensure funds availability to avoid incurring processing fees and risking abandonment or notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle matters with adequate preparation and supervise subordinates (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney must handle legal matters with preparation adequate in the circumstances and must adequately supervise employees tasked with drafting and filing documents before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure example: not supervising an employee who altered a USPTO document (redacting mailing date) and failing to pay an issue fee timely; sanctionable under § 10.77(b). Remedial measures: increased supervisory controls, monitoring, audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter USPTO documents or redact information that impedes client ability to ascertain deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners and their offices must not alter USPTO-issued documents (e.g., removing mailing dates from PTOL-90A cover sheets) in a way that prevents ascertaining the actual due date for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: presenting an Office action with the mailing date redacted, making due date unascertainable and leading to abandonment when no response is filed. If alteration occurred, attorney must remedy consequences and inform affected client(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and produce financial records and client ledgers when requested by OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents must produce documentation showing how client funds were handled (e.g., client ledgers, QuickBooks exports) when OED requests this information in an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page example: Respondent provided a QuickBooks client ledger list for most, but not all, dishonored checks and failed to present documentary evidence showing separation of client funds. Best practice: maintain complete records showing preservation of client funds identity, receipts, deposits, and disbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand priority and timing rules for intent-to-use (ITU) trademark applications (15 U.S.C. § 1057(c); 37 C.F.R. § 2.21(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For ITU applications the priority date is the filing date; if a filing is returned or abandoned due to a dishonored check, the priority date may be lost and a later refiling will have a later priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page example: multiple ITU applications filed with dishonored checks caused applicants to lose an earlier priority date; attorneys must ensure filing fees are actually collected and paid to secure the intended priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 8 and Section 15 submission requirements and timing (15 U.S.C. § 1058 and § 1065)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark registration owners must submit a Section 8 affidavit (specimen, verified statement, required fee) on the six-year anniversary (year prior through up to six months late with surcharge); Section 15 for incontestability requires showing five consecutive years of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely make proper Section 8 submissions within the grace period results in permanent cancellation. Practitioners must collect and timely remit the required fees and filings for clients and avoid dishonored payments that jeopardize registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use USPTO deposit accounts for fee management and include charging instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should maintain a USPTO Deposit Account and include, when paying by deposit account is intended, clear language in correspondence instructing the Office to charge excess or additional amounts to that deposit account and to credit excess fees back to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial measure in order: 'Please charge any additional amounts that may be due in connection with this filing to Deposit Account 504246. Please credit any excess fees to such deposit account.' The Final Order required the Respondent to open a Deposit Account and maintain a minimum balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain minimum deposit account balance (remedial requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a remedial/sanction measure the Respondent opened a USPTO deposit account in which a minimum of $1,000 will be maintained at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational safeguard to avoid future dishonored checks for USPTO fees; considered a best practice when handling client fees for government filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Audit by a Qualified Third Party (remedial/sanction requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must hire, at his own expense, a Qualified Third Party to conduct an Independent Audit of all files on which the implicated employee worked to ensure clients' rights were not adversely affected, and must produce a written Report summarizing the audit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline specified in the order: hire the auditor within 30 days of the Final Order; the auditor must file a written report with the OED Director within seven months; within eight months the practitioner must remedy all adverse consequences identified and provide corroborating documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify affected clients/owners and counsel them about adverse consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When client rights may have been adversely affected (e.g., due to late issue fee payment or document alteration), the practitioner must prepare and send a letter informing the owner/assignee of the factual situation and what occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order required preparation and certified mailing of a letter to the owner/assignee of U.S. Design Patent No. D540,570 advising of the facts surrounding the late issue fee and abandonment/issuance anomaly, and sending a copy of the letter and verification to the OED Director within thirty days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination of Final Order and public discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette and give notice of public discipline to state disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and the public as required by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner obligations: provide copies of the Final Order to state bars within 30 days and file an affidavit with OED within 45 days stating compliance. OED obligations: publish Notice of Stayed Suspension and disseminate per § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedure for noncompliance: Order to Show Cause and lifting stayed suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or disciplinary rules during the stay/probation period, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause why the stay should not be lifted and the respondent suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure in order: send Order to Show Cause to respondent at last address of record; grant fifteen (15) days to respond; after consideration the OED Director may deliver documents to the USPTO Director requesting lifting of the stay and imposition of suspension for up to 36 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay of suspension is lifted and the respondent is suspended, the USPTO will promptly dissociate the respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO, nor may obtain new ones until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of disciplinary proceeding used in future disciplinary contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, will be considered in future complaints as (a) an aggravating factor in determining discipline and/or (b) to rebut statements by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be aware that settlements and Final Orders remain part of professional discipline records and can affect subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision regime during suspension/stay (monitoring and correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of suspension (even if stayed), the respondent must monitor activities of all subordinates and, where a deficiency is noted, correct it immediately and closely monitor the subordinate for 60 days to ensure the deficiency is corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires active supervisory oversight as part of remedial conditions; this is a specific operational expectation and timeframe for post-incident management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation and compliance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement; respondent must provide specified filings and affidavits (e.g., proof of sending Final Order to state bars, proof of audit hiring/reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete deadlines: provide Final Order to state bars within 30 days; file affidavit of compliance within 45 days; auditor report within seven months; remedial steps documented within eight months.
